objective: The acceptance suite of conversations for a problem of several parts (packages 24.6 and 24.8): written people, each played from the first sentence to the one read of the holdout, or to the reason it stays closed, the way the product runs (a draft with the rides and the confirmed cases, the coordinator walking it with the person answering and confirming the map of the problem, the table of accounts attached by name, the plan drawn again from the tables, the programme run, a blocked part dropped when the person says so). Scored on the card (the size, and for one problem its family), the workflow (every part the expert expects is drawn with the expert's approach), the pipeline and the holdout (never worse than the best leaf; closed when the person stops or has no confirmed case). Two arms on the same people: the rules, and the map roles (the decomposer, the map reviewer, the data-need agent, the solution router) served by the model. Dev: six people written beside the rules (not evidence). Sealed: ten people written by an agent given only the three files' columns, the format and the vocabulary, frozen (SHA-256 pinned) before the harness was written; run once. Results: dev JPR-001 (rules, 6 of 6: written beside the rules, not evidence) and JPR-002 (roles, 1 of 6). Sealed, run once on the replica's seed 5: JPR-003 the rules, 2 of 10 right (95% interval 0.057 to 0.51); JPR-004 the roles, 2 of 10, EUR 0.3065; both under the bar (gate journeys_programme_gate_v1: 85% and a lower end of 0.55): fail. The misses: three people with all the files, where the fusion's gain on seed 5 (+0.171, interval -0.092 to +0.512) was not above zero; two people with no confirmed case whom the conversation could not take past the problem card; a single anomaly read as a classification; two single problems drawn as four parts. The set is spent; nothing is tuned on it.
rule: Scores say how DCLab carries these written people over a seeded replica, not how it handles any other person or table, and nothing about production readiness. The dev score is not evidence. The sealed writer is a model instance, not a person: an independent human writer remains the owner's decision. A role serves the product only after the sealed roles arm passed against the rules arm.
